made_by.note: low-band comb fit, octave decided by added-beat support | stems and accents from htdemucs_6s separation, replacing the band-split estimate | mood, novelty and lyrics from MuQ-MuLan, MuQ-large and Whisper

upgrades.note: Derived from numbers already in this file. Nothing was invented, and a field whose source was missing was skipped rather than guessed.

grid.how: onset flux 35-130 Hz, comb search, octave-tested
grid.bar_phase_note: 0-indexed beat of the bar the downbeat falls on. Was 4, which was 1-indexed and disagreed with this map's own downbeats by a quarter note.

refined.how: phase and period chosen where kick energy on the beats peaks in the MIX low band, then required to ALSO rise in the separated drums stem with its 25 ms latency removed
refined.not_applied_to: levels, starlight, dont-look-down: the mix wanted them earlier and the isolated kick disagreed, which is a bass note pulling the optimum, not the beat

is_the_optimum.what: an exhaustive search of every rigid grid on this recording -- period within +/-3% in 0.05% steps, phase in 4 ms steps
is_the_optimum.result: the best rigid grid scores 1.736x on the check's own kick-energy feature. This map's grid scores 1.739x. It is the optimum, to within the resolution of the search.
is_the_optimum.why_the_check_says_0.73: its ceiling is allowed to come from half tempo, and a 42 bpm grid on this record reads 2.00x because the kicks alternate strong and weak and a sparser grid keeps only the strong ones. A grid that skips half the beats is louder per beat and worse at saying where the pulse is.
is_the_optimum.tried_and_reverted: restricting the ceiling to octaves whose beat/off-beat contrast is at least the claimed grid's. It lifted this to 0.99 and then FAILED falsification: a deliberately double-time grid scored 1.00, because a map at the wrong octave can have high contrast at its own octave and so exclude the true one from its own ceiling. Reverted. A hole that lets a real error through is worse than a ceiling that flatters nobody.

sections.note: Which sections are the same section, so a reader can make the second one bigger than the first.
sections.how: boundaries from beat-synchronous band novelty, labelled by kick presence and energy rank; repeat counts occurrences of a label

stems.unit: dB of the stem's RMS over one bar, against the mix's whole-song RMS

accents.how: librosa onset detection per separated stem; the drum stem is split into kick, snare and hat bands before detection
accents.note: the instrument label is now the stem a separator assigned it to, not a guess from the mix
accents.latency_note: Every accent time has been moved -35 ms. The onset detector reports a spectral-flux peak, which arrives after the transient starts, and the lateness showed up the same way on four independent recordings: scored against onset peaks taken from the AUDIO by listen/mapeval.py, all four songs score 0.00 with no correction and peak between -25 and -40 ms (this song: -40). One constant is applied rather than each song's own best, because fitting per song to the check being scored is not a measurement. The per-song optima are kept here so a listening session can settle it properly.

co_timed_claims.not: necessarily an error. kick, snare and hat are frequency splits of ONE drums stem, so a snare hit -- body at 140-900 Hz, transient above 4 kHz -- legitimately appears under two names. It does mean the event count overstates the number of physical hits, which lowers any per-band ceiling computed from it. No dedup rule was applied because any rule chosen now would be chosen against the scorer.

band_validity.how: mean onset-peak alignment of each band's claims against that band's onset envelope in the MIX (low band for kick/bass, above 250 Hz for the rest), divided by the same statistic after jittering every time by up to 90 ms. 1.00 means no better than random.
band_validity.reading: mizhiyoram hat 0.98x: 324 claims, 31% of the list, indistinguishable from noise -- a lofi record's hiss in the 4-12 kHz band read as hi-hats. mizhiyoram kick 1.76x is near-perfect placement.
band_validity.not_pruned: a per-band gate against each band's OWN stem was tried and contradicted this on the very bands in question (mizhiyoram kick 0.28x on its stem, 1.76x on the mix), so it is not trusted and nothing was removed.

timing_offset_considered.what: a global -10 ms shift of every accent time raises listen/mapeval.py's accents check on all five songs (Levels 0.66 -> 0.79, and the same sign and size on the other four)
timing_offset_considered.why_not: the only witness asking for it is the check itself. Measured against spectral-flux peaks in the MIX at 1 ms resolution -- a detector that shares nothing with the check's one-pole band envelope -- our claims already sit within a couple of milliseconds of the event: snare -2.0, kick -2.0, hat -1.0, guitar -3.0, other +1.0, bass -5.0, vocals +0.5, piano +5.0. Moving them 10 ms earlier would take them AWAY from the onsets to sit on the peak of a particular filter, which is a fact about mapeval and not about the record.
timing_offset_considered.what_would_change_my_mind: an independent measurement of the physical attack agreeing that the claims are late. That was attempted against the raw waveform and the test was invalid -- these records have no silence before a hit, so the threshold crossing pinned at the search window edge on every song. A cleaner version would restrict to claims preceded by 100 ms below the 10th percentile of the low band.
timing_offset_considered.worth: about 0.01 of total score, which is not a reason to write a time nobody measured

detector_alternatives_tested.what: replacing every accent with librosa onsets detected per stem -- superflux over a 138-band mel, and a median-aggregated spectral flux
detector_alternatives_tested.result: catastrophically worse on all five songs: 0.00-0.03 against 0.19-0.66 for the accents already in the file, with roughly half as many claims
detector_alternatives_tested.reading: not a selection problem, a timing one. The claims in this file sit within 2 ms of spectral-flux peaks measured on the MIX at 1 ms resolution; a detector whose frame times are the centre of a 1024-point window does not, and no single latency constant made it competitive. Recorded so the next person does not spend the afternoon on it.
detector_alternatives_tested.still_open: the accents check reads 0.19-0.66 because it asks whether each claim is the local maximum of a one-pole band envelope sampled every 5 ms. Our claims are on the onsets. Closing that gap means a better argument about what an accent IS, not a better detector.

retimed_to_attack.how: each claim moved to the last point below 20% of the rise from the local floor to the peak, on its own stem's amplitude envelope smoothed at 60 Hz with a zero-phase filter
retimed_to_attack.why: our claims came from onset flux, and flux and HFC detectors run late against the perceptual attack. The witness they were checked against was also a flux detector, so its agreement proved nothing.
retimed_to_attack.stable: the sign of this correction holds at 10/20/30% thresholds and 40/60/100 Hz smoothing, on every song; only the magnitude moves, because a kick's attack is gradual

stem_levels.note: htdemucs emits six stems whether or not the instrument is in the song. A stem far below the mix is the separator's imagination, and an accent labelled with it is a real transient that bled in from a louder source -- the TIME is measured, the instrument is not. A reader should not light an instrument cue from a stem listed here below about -40 dB.
stem_levels.how: stem RMS against mix RMS, and the share of each label's onsets that fall within 15 ms of an onset on a LOUDER stem

what_was_tried_on_accents.result: raises the check on all five songs
what_was_tried_on_accents.kept: no, then YES via measurement -- see retimed_to_attack; the shift itself was never applied, each claim was moved to its own measured attack

what_was_tried_on_accents.tried: librosa superflux and median spectral flux, per stem, replacing every claim
merging co-timed claims into one event with the others in a `with` field
what_was_tried_on_accents.result: 0.79 -> 0.48 on Levels at a 15 ms window, worse at 10/25/40 ms too. The check's ceiling averages the top-n onsets, so fewer claims raises the bar: density on real onsets is rewarded, and one-event-one-claim is punished

what_was_tried_on_accents.tried: dropping claims from stems below -40 dB re mix (dont-look-down piano at -56 dB, 896 claims)
what_was_tried_on_accents.result: accents WORSE -- 0.72 -> 0.67 -- because those claims sit on the real transient that bled into the stem, so they are correctly timed and only loosely labelled

what_was_tried_on_accents.tried: six variants of the attack measurement (search 60/90 ms, rise 1.15/1.3, envelope 60/120 Hz, max move 30/50 ms)
onsets detected on the MIX added as extra claims
what_was_tried_on_accents.result: 0.79 -> 0.62 on Levels; a crude mix detector's times are worse than stem times corrected to their attack

tonality.how: 1 - spectral flatness over 400-4000 Hz, 512-point window, normalised across the song
tonality.not: not loudness -- this rises when a pitched instrument carries the music, which on a real record often happens as energy falls

melody.how: librosa.pyin on the separated vocals stem, 80-1000 Hz, frame 2048 / hop 256 at 16 kHz; per beat the median voiced f0 over the first quarter of the beat, kept only when mean voicing probability >= 0.50; octave settled on the stem itself (a sung fundamental lives above C3); consecutive beats on one pitch merged into one note
melody.not: every beat. pyin voices 39% of beats here and claims nothing for the rest, which is a smaller and more honest list than autocorrelation produced

superseded.how: autocorrelation f0 on the 80-1000 Hz band of the separated vocals stem

harmony.unit: 0-1, 1 = the chroma turned over completely from the beat before
harmony.how: cosine distance between consecutive 12-bin chroma vectors
harmony.not: not a chord name, and it cannot tell a chord change from a new instrument entering on different notes

voice.unit: 0-1, share of spectral energy carried in the melodic band
voice.not: NOT vocals. This cannot separate a voice from a lead synth or a string line, and it does not read lyrics

chroma.unit: 12 pitch classes, C first, summing to 1
chroma.how: mean of the per-beat chroma over 250-2000 Hz
chroma.not: not a chord and not a scale -- it is where this song puts its pitched energy across the twelve names

key.how: Krumhansl-Schmuckler: song-mean 12-bin chroma correlated against the 24 rotated key profiles, best match wins
key.not: not a modulation-aware key. A song that changes key gets whichever key it spends most of its energy in. A key and its relative share all seven notes, so when those two score alike this cannot tell them apart and says so by dropping confidence rather than picking

mood.unit: 0-1 per term across the song, so a section can be MORE euphoric than another
mood.how: MuQ-MuLan-large joint music/text embedding, up to 10 s from each section compared against a fixed vocabulary
mood.not: not a colour and not an instruction. It says where the music sits among these words; what a rig does about that is the reader's business

novelty.unit: 0-1, 1 = the biggest change in this song
novelty.how: cosine distance between MuQ-large frame embeddings averaged over one bar either side
novelty.not: not loudness. This rises where the music CHANGES, which is often where nothing gets louder

lyrics.how: Whisper small with word timestamps, on the separated vocal stem
lyrics.not: the words are unreliable on a sung separated stem; the TIMES are what a reader should trust

grid_check.against: kick onsets from the separated drum stem
grid_check.note: Negative means the kick lands BEFORE the beat the grid names, so the grid is LATE by that much; positive means the grid is early. This is two measurements of one recording by different methods, not truth: the onset detector carries its own bias and nobody has verified either against a human ear. Recorded so a reader or a listening session can see it, never applied as a correction.
grid_check.priced: moving the whole grid by -15 ms takes levels' hitters from 50.3% to 56.9% within 40 ms of their own instrument. Measured, not applied: it is the same kick onsets this offset was measured against, so it is not independent evidence

chords.how: ChordMini BTC large-vocabulary model (170 classes; ptnghia-j/ChordMini, MIT) on the mix, CQT 144 bins / 24 per octave, hop 2048 at 22.05 kHz. Per bar: the segment covering the downbeat. `segments` holds the model's own boundaries.
chords.not: checked against an instrument by anyone here. It is a model trained on human chord annotations, which is a different thing from a human, and 'N' bars carry no chord rather than a guess
chords.covers: the share of the bar this chord actually occupies, from the model's own segment boundaries. It replaces a hardcoded confidence of 0.8 that was on every event in every map -- a number nobody measured, in a field called confidence. This one is measured: a bar split between two chords reads below 1.0, and the label names only the chord at the downbeat.

phrases.how: runs of words separated by more than 0.57 s of silence (0.8 beats at this tempo, floored at 0.30 s)
phrases.not: this is where the voice is, not what it says. The word text is the unreliable half of the source and none of it is used here

structure_check.how: novelty local maxima at or above 60% of this song's biggest change, matched to chapter boundaries within two bars
structure_check.not: neither side is truth and this does not say which is wrong where they disagree. chapters are not edited from this: a model does not overwrite a measurement, and one fact keeps one writer. A median gap of 0.00 s is NOT precision: novelty is sampled per downbeat and chapters land on downbeats, so both are already on the same grid and an exact match is the only thing a hit can look like

pump.how: envelope above 250 Hz so the kick body is excluded, measured from 18% to 72% of each beat so neither the kick's attack nor the next one is in the window. Music without sidechain DECAYS between hits; music with it RISES, because the compressor is letting go. The sign of that slope is the whole test. Calibrated on records that cannot pump: the synthetic ladder is additive synthesis with no compressor in it, and comes out negative.

groove.how: deviation of each drum hit from the nearest sixteenth, in beats, kept per hit as off16. A quantised record reads near zero on every slot; swing shows as a consistent bias on the off-slots. This is the information snapT was overwriting.

instruments.how: derived from stems.sources, which is htdemucs presence per bar. enters and leaves use two thresholds, 42% and 26% of that stem's own peak, so a percentile, so one loud bar cannot set the bar for the whole song. No new listening was done and no stem audio was used -- every number here is a function of the per-bar levels already in this file.

vocal_silence.how: stems.vocals below 0.12, runs of two seconds or more
vocal_silence.note: Where the voice is absent. The cleanest structural signal in most records, and what lets a reader spotlight a singer who is actually singing.

microtiming.unit: ms from the nearest 1/16 of a beat
microtiming.how: deviation of each accent from the nearest sixteenth
microtiming.note: Measured against the grid the music is actually played on. Measuring against the nearest BEAT instead reports half a beat of scatter and calls it feel, which is an artifact of assigning subdivision hits to beats.

chords_check.between: observations.chords and a second, independent chord estimate
chords_check.how: observations.chords is chroma template matching over 250-2000 Hz of the full mix (listen/ear.py). The second is per-semitone Goertzel energy C2-C7 folded to twelve classes, matched against maj/min/dom7 (listen/harmony.py). Different front ends, same audio.
chords_check.verdict: DISPUTED. Two methods agree on the chord in 11% of bars and on even the root in 21%. That is not a small disagreement, and nothing here says which one is right. A reader should treat observations.chords as a weak signal until a human with an instrument settles it (truth/PROTOCOL.md).

superseded.what: observations.chords was the full-mix chroma estimate; it is now the stem estimate
superseded.old_how: chroma template match over 250-2000 Hz of the FULL MIX, 36 templates (maj, min, dom7), mode-smoothed across 3 bars
superseded.new_how: chroma over the separated bass+piano+guitar+other stems, with the root taken from observations.bass_notes and only the quality matched (maj, min, 7, m7, sus4)
superseded.why: three estimates existed and the two full-mix ones agreed with each other on 11-31% of bars. The stem estimate reads only the stems that carry harmony, so no kick drum sits in its chroma, and its root is measured on the isolated bass rather than inferred. It agrees with that root on 61% of the bars it names, by construction.

superseded_stem_estimate.how: chroma over the separated bass+piano+guitar+other stems, with the root taken from observations.bass_notes and only the quality matched (maj, min, 7, m7, sus4)
superseded_stem_estimate.why: a chord model trained on human annotations beat the stem-chroma estimate on the audio check on three of four songs and tied on the fourth, and its labels on Levels are the record's actual progression

stereo.how: mid/side on the STEREO source decoded straight from the release, not from synth/out which is mono 32 kHz and cannot carry this. width = |S|/(|M|+|S|) with M=(L+R)/2, S=(L-R)/2
stereo.not: a stereo measurement of a mix, not of any instrument. A wide bar says the production opened up, not which part moved
stereo.source: Mizhiyoram -  Manjil Virinja Pookkal  Lofi Mix  Prazz Mu6.mp3

bass_notes.how: autocorrelation f0 on the 38-420 Hz band of the separated bass stem
bass_notes.not: the note the BASS is playing, which is not always the root of the chord and never the chord itself. A beat whose autocorrelation peak is below 0.34 is null rather than the nearest note

melody_centroid.unit: 0-1, where the pitched line sits between this song's own lowest and highest fifth-percentile centroid
melody_centroid.how: energy-weighted log-frequency centroid over 250-2000 Hz per beat
melody_centroid.not: not the note being sung -- this is where the pitched energy sits, and a chord moves it as surely as a melody does
melody_centroid.renamed_from: observations.melody. It is a spectral centroid, not a note, and melody now carries the sung note like the-nights and listen/mapeval.py both expect

stem_latency.of: htdemucs_6s output against the mix it was separated from
stem_latency.how: cross-correlation of the drums stem envelope against the source mix envelope, 4 kHz, +/-100 ms search, 20 s window
stem_latency.why_it_matters: Every field derived from a stem inherits it: accents, bass_notes, melody, brightness, envelope and the per-bar stem levels all come from audio that runs 25 ms behind the record. It is the same number on all four songs, so it is the separator and not the music.
stem_latency.already_applied_to: accents, via accents.latency_correction_s of -35 ms, which is this 25 ms plus roughly 10 ms of onset-detector flux latency
stem_latency.not: applied to bass_notes or melody. Compensating the sampling point there made both measurably worse against listen/mapeval.py, so the sign or the mechanism is not what I assumed and the correction is recorded rather than applied.

also_measured_by.who: the-nights map (teammate), independently, on a different song
also_measured_by.agreement: 0.08 ms apart from a separate implementation on a fifth recording; two writers, one number, so this is the separator not a bug in either measurement

downbeats_suspect.what: the beat this map calls the bar line is not the loudest beat of the bar. Slot 3 is, on all four songs we measured.
downbeats_suspect.how: mean band energy at every beat, folded into four slots using this map's own grid.bar_phase, slot 0 being the claimed bar line
downbeats_suspect.not_evidence: chord changes land on slot 0 100% of the time and that proves nothing -- chords are estimated PER BAR, at downbeat times, so the agreement is by construction. Grading a thing against its own output is the first mistake listed in this repo and it is easy to repeat.
downbeats_suspect.unresolved: the loudest beat of a bar is not always the bar line, and vocal phrase starts disagree across songs (slot 3 on starlight, slot 1 on dont-look-down) because singers come in on a pickup. Nothing here settles it. A human with the audio does, under truth/PROTOCOL.md.
downbeats_suspect.related: a teammate found drops two beats early on the-nights by ear, and a rotated copy of these downbeats scores higher than the true one on the harness -- both point at the same question.

more_witnesses.reading: every energy band and where the singer starts held notes put the weight of the bar on slots 2-3; the map's bar line is on the quiet half. Moving the bar line alone scores downbeats 1.00 and collapses bars to 0.00; moving the chapters with it drops sections 1.00 -> 0.62 because the audio genuinely changes where the chapters are now.
more_witnesses.conclusion: two audio-based checks disagree by one beat about where the bar begins and no measurement here breaks the tie. Not rotated. This is what truth/PROTOCOL.md is for.

beat_this_grid_trial.what: the whole grid replaced by beat_this's beats and downbeats (171 beats, 44 downbeats, period 0.720, bar_phase 1), structure remapped to its nearest beats, scored with listen/mapeval.py
beat_this_grid_trial.reading: its bar line IS the bar accent the check hears -- downbeats 0.00 -> 1.00 -- and its beats sit half a beat from the kick, so grid 0.91 -> 0.08. mapeval defines the beat as where the kick is; a tracker trained on human tapping defines it as where people tap. On this syncopated record those are half a beat apart, and no grid satisfies both.
beat_this_grid_trial.decision: not applied. The map keeps the kick-aligned grid and carries this so a reader knows the bar line is disputed by a human-trained tracker.

beat_tracker_check.how: its beats and downbeats against this map's grid: which of OUR four bar slots its downbeats land on, and the median offset of our beats from its nearest beat
beat_tracker_check.beat_phase_vs_ours: +0.40 of a beat, spread 0.19, same period (0.720 vs 0.714)
beat_tracker_check.reading: it hears the BEAT half a beat from ours. Our kicks sit on our beats, so if the tracker is right the kick is syncopated and our grid is on the offbeat -- which would explain the bar energy on slots 2-3, downbeats scoring 0.00, and sections disagreeing with the energy. Leading hypothesis. Not applied: a half-beat move would put the grid off the kicks, which is what listen/mapeval.py grid measures, so the scorer and a human tracker disagree about what a beat IS on a syncopated record.
beat_tracker_check.note_on_offset: our beats run 29-45 ms EARLY against it on the three songs where the beat agrees. A human-trained tracker marks the onset; our grid sits at the kick's peak energy, which mapeval's grid check rewards. Two definitions of 'the beat' about 30 ms apart. Recorded, not applied.

phrase_grid.how: every phrase length in [2, 4, 8, 16] bars and every offset scored against the novelty peaks; the best-supported one wins
phrase_grid.not: this is the FINEST boundary grid the music supports, not the phrase length a musician would name. A 2-bar grid contains every 4-bar mark, so support can only rise as the grid gets finer, and scoring against chance narrows that bias without removing it. Read it as: the song offers a boundary here this often. Four bars is the pop default and a default written down is indistinguishable from a measurement, which is why nothing is assumed and a grid beating chance by less than 0.35 is not written at all

notes.how: Spotify basic-pitch (ICASSP 2022) via the ONNX backend, polyphonic, per stem, onset 0.55 / frame 0.35 / min 70 ms; start times moved 25 ms earlier to take out the separator's measured latency (observations.stem_latency)
notes.note: a model's transcription of a separated stem, not a score. Amplitude is the model's, not dB. Drums are not here because a kick is not a pitch.

moment_timing.how: each drop and stop moved to the beat carrying the biggest sustained step in loudness within two bars, the step being the median across 0.5, 1.0, 1.5 and 2.0 s shoulders
moment_timing.why: ear.py builds moments from section boundaries and section boundaries are bar lines, so a drop that lands on a half bar was pushed to the next full bar -- two beats late, every time
moment_timing.second_witness: drum hits per beat, counted from the separated stems, which shares no arithmetic with the loudness envelope

bar_phase_decision.decided_by: the low band on bar lines against the other beats, measured on this recording -- bar lines 2.43x the other beats
bar_phase_decision.why_not_the_old_one: the previous phase put the bar line on the quietest beat of the four. The evidence for it was that the chapters agreed with it, and ear.py builds chapters AT the bar phase, so that agreement was arithmetic rather than evidence.
bar_phase_decision.what_moved: chapters, spans and section entries, which are derived from the bar line. Moments did not: they are measured from the recording by listen/moments.py and shifting them made them worse.
bar_phase_decision.dissent: harmonic change and bass note changes on this record favour a phase two beats away -- a half bar. The kick and the chord change disagree, as they do on Levels, and only an ear settles which one begins the bar.

meter.how: hits per beat on kick, snare and hat as a 3-vector per beat; mean cosine similarity at every lag out to 16 beats; each candidate judged on itself and its multiples, since a bar of N peaks at N, 2N and 3N
meter.why_recorded: beats_per_bar=4 is a default argument in ear.py that nothing has ever checked, and every downbeat, chapter and bar-phase argument in this repo rests on it
meter.not: not the notated time signature. It is the period the DRUMS repeat on, which is what a reader needs and what ear.py assumes is four. A song whose drums and score disagree will read here as the drums.
meter.measured_how: self-similarity of the drum pattern at each candidate lag, judged on the lag and its double. This is a PERCUSSIVE measurement, so it must not be checked against another percussive one -- mapeval's ev_meter checks it against the spacing of the chord changes instead, which comes from a harmonic model sharing no code with this path.

surprise.unit: 0-1, 1 = the biggest departure in this song
surprise.how: each bar's MERT row, pooled and L2-normalised, against the mean of the four bars before it; the surprise is the cosine distance. The rows are unit vectors, so the loudness of the bar is divided out before anything is compared.
surprise.why_it_exists: a reader that only knows what is loud answers a drop and misses the moment a record does something it has not done before, which is often quiet.
surprise.not_from_loudness: deliberately. The previous version of this field predicted a bar from its hit counts, its six stem LEVELS and its energy, and correlated -0.47 to -0.52 with the bar's own loudness across the five songs -- a quiet bar after loud ones was being called surprising for being quiet. mapeval now refuses this field if that correlation returns.
surprise.not: not a claim that a listener is surprised. It is that a model trained on a lot of music did not see this bar coming from the four before it.
surprise.checked_against: its own correlation with loudness, in mapeval.ev_surprise, which is an upper bound rather than a target
surprise.no_positive_check: no independent check for this field survived. Whether surprise rises in bars introducing a chord the previous four did not contain -- harmony being symbolic and from another model -- gave lifts of +0.09, -0.03, -0.03, +0.05, +0.11 across the five songs: three positive, two negative, none large. The field is a measurement with a guard against the way it used to be wrong, and no evidence that it is right.

grid_crosscheck.what: the bar line and the tempo octave, checked against harmony instead of drums
grid_crosscheck.why: grid.bar_phase comes from where the drum pattern repeats and listen/meter.py confirms beats-per-bar from the same drum pattern, which is drums grading drums. Chord boundaries come from ChordMini, a harmonic model that shares no code and no feature family with the percussive path, and a chord change lands on a bar line far more often than not.

tempo_octave_from_harmony.verdict: harmonic rhythm sits on whole beats, consistent with the claimed tempo

grid_crosscheck.not: this does not pick a winner. A disagreement means the bar line is not settled, and the honest response is to say so in confidence rather than to choose silently between two methods that each have a case.

confidence_downbeats.why: harmony puts the bar line on phase 1 and this file claims 2

derivable_fields_removed.note: four fields were removed from this file because a reader can compute them from what is already here: anticipation (how far to the next moment, from `moments`), remaining (how much of this section or span is left, a subtraction), arc (where the energy curve peaks, its argmax) and lead (which stem is carrying the bar, a comparison between series in `stems`). Carrying them twice meant two copies free to disagree, and they did: Levels' anticipation still pointed at drop times that listen/moments.py had since re-measured. They are computed in ONE place now, readers/src/derive.js, which reproduces every one of the 489 rows this file used to carry.

pan.how: (R energy - L energy) / (R + L) over 40 ms from the accent, on the stereo stem that accent's label belongs to, with the +25 ms separator latency correction applied
pan.why_it_exists: accents say a hat was struck; they do not say the hat is on the right. A reader that can place anything to the left or the right of the audience cannot decide which side answers a hit without this, and defaulting to the middle throws away every left-right decision the record already made.
pan.not: a claim about where the instrument was recorded. It is where the mix puts it, which is a production decision and can change between sections.
pan.source: stereo stems separated from the release file, NOT from synth/out, which is a mono downmix for four of these five songs and cannot carry pan
pan.checked_against: the raw release mix's own L-R at the same instants, in mapeval.ev_pan. Shares the recording and no code: one side is six separated stereo files, the other is the unseparated release.

attack.wanted: per bar: is this bar percussive and hitty, or smooth and sustained, so a reader can choose between stabbing and flowing without inferring it from loudness
attack.why_null: two candidate writers and three candidate checks were built and no pair of them agrees. A number written here would be one nobody could corroborate, which is the one thing this file is not allowed to contain.

what_was_tried.instrument: envelope flux ratio -- the share of a bar's energy that arrives as a positive jump in the broadband envelope
what_was_tried.result: has range, but is uncorrelated with the HPSS percussive share (r = -0.25 to +0.36 across the five songs), so the two disagree about which bars are percussive

what_was_tried.instrument: harmonic-percussive source separation (librosa, margin 2.0), percussive share of bar energy
what_was_tried.result: not a loudness proxy, which is the right property (r with bar loudness -0.35 to +0.28), but almost no range on these masters: 0.00-0.05 on mizhiyoram and 0.00-0.31 on levels. A track with an obvious drum pattern reading 5% percussive is the measurement failing, not the track

what_was_tried.instrument: phase deviation of complex one-pole resonators at six octaves
what_was_tried.result: measures signal-to-noise, not transients: correlation with envelope flux came out -0.38, -0.42, +0.40 on three songs. Sign not even stable

what_was_tried.instrument: Bello phase deviation on a proper 256-point STFT, 24 sampled bars per song
what_was_tried.result: sign still unstable across songs: +0.51, -0.53, +0.17, +0.03, +0.26. Phase deviation rises for transients AND for broadband noise, and falls for steady tones however loud, so it cannot separate a percussive bar from a noisy one
consistent in sign at last but the WRONG sign -- percussive bars should be less periodic, and correlation with flux came out +0.23, +0.45, +0.25, +0.15, -0.07. Dominated by density

attack.the_likely_cause: synth/out is a mono 32 kHz downmix of a heavily limited commercial master for four of the five songs. Limiting flattens exactly the crest-factor difference between a hit and a pad, which is the property this field is named after. Measuring it may need a source that has not been through that.
attack.what_would_settle_it: a recording with an unlimited transient response, or a percussiveness estimate from the separated drum stem's own envelope against the harmonic stems', which is not the same as HPSS on the mix and was not tried

space.wanted: per section: direct-to-reverberant, so a reader can open the room up when the record does
space.why_null: the ratio is measurable and does vary, but it is not a property of the section, which is the rate the field is defined at. Two sections with the same name disagree about as much as the whole song varies.

what_was_tried.instrument: energy 100-250 ms after an isolated accent, over the energy at +30 ms, median per section, using only accents with no other accent inside the tail window
what_was_tried.result: varies 0.23 to 1.42 across sections within a song, and is NOT a loudness artefact (r with local loudness -0.11 to -0.15). But the same-named sections disagree: levels' three breaks read 0.71/0.69/0.84 and its four drops 0.86/0.92/0.72/0.82, a same-name spread of 0.18 against a whole-song spread of 0.24. The Nights' four drops read 0.50/0.95/0.45/0.71, nearly the full range of the song. On two of five songs the same-name spread is 70%+ of the total

what_was_tried.instrument: the same ratio read as reverberation directly
what_was_tried.result: gives the wrong answer where the answer is known: The Nights' intro reads 0.97 and its drops 0.45-0.50, so the sparse reverberant intro measures DRIER than the dense drops. What the window actually contains in a drop is sidechain ducking -- which this file already measures, as observations.pump -- and other instruments sustaining, not a decay tail

space.the_likely_cause: a post-onset window in dense music contains everything else that is playing. Isolating a decay needs the gaps, and a limited master has no gaps.
space.what_would_settle_it: measure the tail on the separated drum stem, where the gaps between hits are real gaps, and correct for the ducking depth already in observations.pump. Both are available and neither was tried

spans_decode.how: semi-Markov Viterbi over four-bar boundaries. States flat, build, quiet; duration prior cheapest at 8 and 16 bars, refused below 4 and above 32; transition costs make build->build expensive and build->flat free.
spans_decode.features: how many stems are within 12 dB of their own 90th percentile (a count), the share of bar energy held by anything that is not drums or bass, the drums' own share, and chord changes per bar. None of these is the energy curve, and two of them cannot move when the volume does.
spans_decode.not: not derived from anything in this file a reader could read. The old spans were a greedy walk over `energy` and by rule 3 had no business being written down at all.
spans_decode.boundaries: four-bar multiples, applied inside the decode rather than snapped afterwards
spans_decode.checked_against: the energy composite of section 1a -- onset rate, high-band onset rate and band occupancy on the raw mix -- with randomly placed spans of the same durations as the control. Shares the recording and no feature.

identity.unit: the index of the earlier bar this one is the same material as, or null
identity.how: MERT rows pooled per bar and L2-normalised, then the nearest earlier bar by cosine. The bar must beat this song's own 97% pair similarity (0.854 here, against a median of 0.688), and sit at least 2 bars back so the previous bar does not count as a repeat.
identity.why_not_a_fixed_threshold: every bar of one song sits close to every other in this embedding. A fixed 0.55 matched 125 of Levels' 127 bars to something, which is not a measurement of anything.
identity.why_it_exists: sections says a passage is the second 'drop'. It does not say bar 97 is the same music as bar 33, which is what a reader needs to answer a repeat the way it answered the first time, or deliberately not.
identity.not: not a claim that the two bars are identical audio. It is that a model trained on a great deal of music puts them in the same place, which is closer to what a listener means by 'this bit again' than a waveform comparison would be.
identity.reads_nothing_else: not sections, not chapters, not energy. If this and sections disagree, both were arrived at independently.
identity.checked_against: chord-sequence repetition, in mapeval.ev_identity -- a symbolic label from a different model, sharing the recording and no code

percentile.wanted: where this song sits against other songs -- busier than 80% of them, slower than 60% -- so a reader can tell a restrained record from a relentless one without being told what normal is
percentile.why_null: the corpus is five songs. A percentile over five is quantised to 20-point steps before anything else goes wrong, and the check the brief asked for -- rank stability across a corpus split -- fails outright.

what_was_tried.instrument: percentile of five per-song scalars (bpm, accents per second, mean energy, energy range, drops per minute) over the five-song corpus, with the corpus resampled 200 times
what_was_tried.result: every one of the five features moves 40 percentile points between the 10th and 90th resample. A number that swings 40 points is not a fact about the song, it is a fact about which four songs happened to be in the corpus

percentile.the_likely_cause: five songs, four of them 126-128 bpm dance records and one lofi cover at 84. There is no corpus here to be relative to.
percentile.what_would_settle_it: more songs. The resample swing falls roughly as one over the square root of the corpus size, so getting from 40 points to 10 needs something like 80 songs -- an estimate from that scaling, not a measurement. The field is cheap to fill the moment a corpus exists: the writer is five lines and the check is the bootstrap already written here.

weight.wanted: how much this record MEANS to the people who will be in the room -- the difference between the drop everybody has been waiting for and a drop in a song nobody knows
weight.why_null: the check the brief asked for is the one that failed. Two crowd sources were queried and they cannot be made to agree on which record they are describing, so there is nothing to average and nothing to corroborate.

what_was_tried.instrument: MusicBrainz recording search, artist and title
what_was_tried.result: 130 matching recordings for Avicii's Levels, 14 for Don't Look Down, 0 for Mizhiyoram, and two of the five queries timed out. Hit count is a measure of how often a track has been re-released, which is not what this field is asking

resolved 'Levels' to the article 'Level', a 29-character disambiguation stub, and 'Don't Look Down' to an unrelated page. Only The Nights resolved to the right record. A source that identifies the wrong entity is worse than no source, because the number it produces looks exactly like a real one

weight.the_likely_cause: neither source is keyed on anything this file holds. Matching by artist and title is ambiguous by construction, and one of these five is a lofi cover with no canonical release at all.
weight.what_would_settle_it: an identifier rather than a title -- an ISRC or a MusicBrainz recording MBID stored in `song`, resolved once by a human and then used to key every external lookup. That is a small piece of work and it is the whole blocker; everything after it is arithmetic.
weight.and_a_caution: this is the one field in the file whose source is outside the recording. Whatever fills it will be a claim about a population, measured at a moment, that changes without the song changing -- so it needs a date attached in a way none of the other fields do.

idiom.wanted: which conventions this record is working inside, so a reader can know that a bar of silence before a drop is a genre convention being honoured rather than the song stopping
idiom.why_null: no check exists that is not circular. Every candidate compares the record against a model or a corpus that would have to encode the same conventions to judge them, and with five songs there is no corpus to encode them from.

what_was_tried.instrument: the MuLan mood embedding already in observations.mood
what_was_tried.result: it produces genre-like labels, but grading them means comparing a model's genre labels against a model's genre labels. That is the circular verification this whole piece of work exists to remove, and adding it back for a field nobody has asked a reader to use would be the worst trade in the file

idiom.the_likely_cause: an idiom is a fact about a body of music, and this repository has five songs, four of which are the same idiom.
idiom.what_would_settle_it: a corpus with labelled idioms and a held-out split, which is the same blocker as `percentile` and would be solved by the same corpus

restraint.wanted: where the record is deliberately holding back -- not quiet, HELD. A reader that cannot tell the two apart spends everything in the first minute
restraint.why_null: the brief allows this field STATED provenance only, and nobody has stated it. That is not a gap to be filled by a measurement; a measurement here would be the wrong kind of answer and this field refuses one by design.
restraint.how_it_gets_filled: a human listens and says so, through listen/corrections.py, which is why that tool was built first. The entry carries who said it and why, and provenance stays 'stated' -- it never becomes 'measured' by being written down.

what_was_tried.instrument: low energy with high harmonic activity -- quiet bars that are still doing something
what_was_tried.result: not tried against the audio, and deliberately. It would produce a number with provenance 'measured' for a field the brief says may only be 'stated', and a measured-looking number is exactly what makes a human judgment impossible to find later

restraint.what_would_settle_it: one person, one pass through one song, and an entry in the corrections log. It is the cheapest unsolved field here and the only one that needs no code at all

latent.wanted: room for what a learned head finds that nobody has named yet
latent.why_null: empty on purpose, and labelled empty on purpose. The brief says ship it empty; the reason it is worth shipping empty is that an empty labelled field tells a reader the slot exists and is unclaimed, where an absent field tells it nothing. Anything put here now would be one of the measurements already in this file wearing a name that promises more.

what_was_tried.result: no attempt was made, which is the correct amount of attempt. There is no head trained yet, and the vectors it would be trained from are in the sidecar and already referenced

latent.what_would_settle_it: a trained head, and the one thing to get right when it arrives is that whatever it emits goes here under a name that does not claim to be a musical fact until somebody has checked it against one

hook.why_null: whisper-small returns nothing usable from this recording. On the separated vocal it produced zero segments both with automatic language detection (which reported English) and with Malayalam given explicitly. On the raw mix with Malayalam given it produced 15 segments and 40 words, and the words are hallucinated -- the transcript mixes Korean and Chinese glyphs into invented English phrases. A hook found in that would be a fabricated number that looks exactly like a measured one, so it is not written.
what_was_tried: separated vocal, language auto-detected: detected English, 0 segments
raw mix, language=ml: 15 segments, 40 words, and the text is not Malayalam or anything else
hook.what_would_settle_it: a larger Whisper checkpoint, or a transcriber trained for Malayalam. The hook is audible and repeated in this song -- a listener finds it in one pass -- so this is a tooling gap and not a property of the record. It is also a case where `restraint`'s route applies: a human could state it through listen/corrections.py today.
hook.model: openai-whisper small, on the separated vocal stem and on the raw mix

position.how: pos is beats from the grid origin: seconds = grid.phase + pos * grid.period. bar and beat are DERIVED from pos and grid.bar_phase and are never stored, because a stored derived value is how two fields get to disagree about where a bar begins.

vectors.revision_provenance: measured -- the commit this machine's huggingface cache holds for that model
vectors.provenance: measured -- rows, bytes and sha256 read off the file on disk
vectors.pooling: mean of 75.0 Hz frames between consecutive beats, then L2-normalised
vectors.not: a fact a human can check by ear. It is what a large model heard, for a small head to learn from. Also: this torch build renamed the weight-norm parametrisation, so the positional-conv weights of the checkpoint did not load and are randomly initialised; embeddings are slightly perturbed from the published model's. the-nights' vectors were made the same way.
vectors.note: a reference, not the data. The vectors are in the file named here, beside this map. The name carries the model and the revision that produced it so a different checkpoint cannot overwrite it, and the sha256 and byte count are measured from the file on disk so a reference that has gone stale can be caught instead of trusted.
vectors.how_to_read: numpy.fromfile(file, dtype='<f2').reshape(rows, dim); row i is beat i of `beats`, L2-normalised, so a dot product between two rows is a cosine

energy_note: energy rows re-snapped to this map's downbeats after the bar line moved: 43 of 43 rows, largest move 31 ms. Values untouched.

corrections.note: Every change a human made to this file: when, which field, what it said, what it says now, and why. Not a description of the song -- a record of where we described it wrongly. It is the only field here that cannot be derived from anything else, and the only one that makes restraint, weight and latent reachable: those three need examples of human judgment overriding a measurement, and this is where those examples accumulate. Append-only. A correction is testimony, not measurement, so there is nothing to check it against -- the schema is validated strictly instead, and an entry is never rewritten or removed.

entries.why: the claimed bar line carried 0.48x the low-band energy of the other beats -- the bar began where the kick was quietest, and the evidence for it was that chapters agreed with it, which is arithmetic because ear.py builds chapters AT the bar phase

entries.was: null -- 'the transcriber was pointed at the wrong language, which is fixable'
entries.now: null -- whisper-small hallucinates on this recording even with Malayalam given
entries.why: I wrote the first reason before testing it. Giving the language explicitly still returns zero segments from the vocal stem, and the raw mix returns 40 words of invented text mixing Korean and Chinese glyphs. The reason I published was a guess about my own tooling
